item.title: American Academy in Berlin: Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027-28
item.description:
Organisation: American Academy in Berlin

Location: Berlin, Germany, at the Hans Arnhold Center. RESTRICTED: fellowships are open only to citizens and permanent residents of the United States.

Award: Monthly stipend of USD 5,000, plus roundtrip airfare, accommodation at or near the Hans Arnhold Center, partial board, in-house library services and professional networking opportunities. Roughly two dozen fellowships awarded each year. No application fee.

Duration: One full academic semester (about 4 months). Fall runs mid-August to mid-December; spring runs late January to late May.

Deadline: 25 Sep 2026

The American Academy in Berlin is an independent, nonprofit institute for advanced study in the arts, humanities, social sciences, law, journalism and public policy, whose primary mission is to strengthen the cultural and intellectual ties between the United States and Germany. Each year, after a rigorous selection process, the Academy awards roughly two dozen semester-long Berlin Prize fellowships to individuals who demonstrate excellence in their fields. DISCIPLINES: applications are welcome across the humanities, social sciences, law, journalism and various areas of public policy. The Academy generally encourages projects addressing pressing issues of the day, specifically naming democracy, security, technology and society (especially AI), energy including climate, and global order. Dedicated fellowships also support projects in Jewish studies, German studies, and public health and biotechnology. Project proposals need not focus on Germany, but candidates should explain how a residency in Berlin would enhance their work. NOT ACCEPTED: proposals in mathematics or the natural sciences. NOTE FOR ARTISTS: visual artists and composers are invited through separate, nomination-based competitions, so there is no open application route for them here. ELIGIBILITY: fellowships are restricted to citizens and permanent residents of the United States. Both emerging and established figures are eligible. PhD holders qualify as emerging scholars with a strong record of peer-reviewed work beyond the dissertation; candidates in non-academic fields such as journalism, filmmaking and policy need a significant record of publication or production; fiction and nonfiction writers must have published at least one book with a reputable press. WHAT FELLOWS DO: fellows present their work to audiences in and around Berlin through lectures, readings, public discussions, performances and film screenings, and should be willing to engage with relevant German institutions, organizations and the media; these activities are integral to the Academy's mission of fostering transatlantic dialogue. APPLICATION MATERIALS: a project proposal of 1,500 to 1,750 words plus a one-page bibliography; a curriculum vitae of up to 10 pages; two writing samples totalling no more than 60 pages; and three letters of recommendation, which are due 2 October 2026. DEADLINE: Friday 25 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Eastern Time (18:00 Central European Time). TIMELINE: all candidates are notified of the competition outcome by email in late March 2027; the 2027-28 Berlin Prize recipients are announced in May 2027.

item.title: Translation House Looren: Translators' Residencies and Pro Helvetia Stipends 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Uebersetzerhaus Looren

Location: Wernetshausen, Switzerland (Zurich region)

Award: Free residency stay (apartments at the translation house). Six competitive CHF 4,000 translation grants per year, each tied to a one-month residency. Pro Helvetia residency programme separately funded. James Joyce Scholarship and Looren Residency 2027 has its own conditions. No application fee.

Duration: Stays of typically 2 weeks to 2 months; CHF 4,000 stipend grants tied to one-month residencies

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

Translators' residency at Uebersetzerhaus Looren in Wernetshausen near Zurich. Looren offers a free residency for literary translators with a current contract, including six competitive CHF 4,000 stipend grants per year tied to one-month residencies. The Pro Helvetia residency programme (separately funded) has a 2026-10-15 deadline for 2027 stays. The James Joyce Scholarship and Looren Residency 2027 closes 2026-10-31. General free residencies are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year. ELIGIBILITY: literary translators with substantial published work and a current translation contract; any language combination is welcome. Apply via the application page on looren.net. No application fee.

Open call details

item.title: Tartu UNESCO City of Literature Residency for Writers and Translators, Autumn 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Estonian Literary Society (Eesti Kirjanduse Selts), Focal Point for Tartu UNESCO City of Literature

Location: Tartu, Estonia. Open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature worldwide.

Award: Monthly stipend of EUR 600 for the two-month stay (EUR 1,200 in total), plus reimbursement of travel costs up to EUR 350. Free accommodation is provided in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment, which has a bedroom, living room, kitchen, bathroom and exhibition room. One resident is selected. No application fee.

Duration: Two months, 15 October to 15 December 2026, with some flexibility on exact dates

Deadline: Closed 01 Sep 2026

The Estonian Literary Society, which coordinates Tartu UNESCO City of Literature, runs an international residency programme for writers and translators that has hosted authors from Slovenia, Ireland, Hungary, the USA, the UK, Ukraine and Canada since 2017. This is the open call for the autumn 2026 slot: one resident stays two months in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment in Tartu, working on their own writing or translation while connecting with the local literary scene. WHAT THE RESIDENCY OFFERS: a EUR 600 monthly stipend, travel reimbursement up to EUR 350, free accommodation, a local support coordinator to help arrange cultural engagements, and opportunities to perform and present at literary events. The autumn period covers the interdisciplinary literary festival Crazy Tartu on 12 to 14 November, and the resident is offered a slot to perform there alongside writers, poets, musicians and artists from Estonia and abroad. ELIGIBILITY: open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature of any nationality; applicants need an upper-intermediate level of spoken English, at least one published book, screenplay, theatre script or translation from Estonian into another language, a demonstrable interest in Estonian culture and literature, a willingness to take part in local literary activities, and a commitment to working on their own literary project during the stay. HOW TO APPLY: complete the online application form linked from the residency page and upload a fragment of up to five pages of a published text (in Estonian or English) or of a published translation. SELECTION: made by a committee representing the Estonian Literary Society, the Estonian Writers Union, the Estonian Literary Museum and the Tartu Literature House Foundation. Results are announced before 15 September 2026. The programme's stated aims are to enhance international exchange, diversify the local literary scene, introduce new foreign authors and their work to Estonian readers, and build lasting connections beyond the residency period. Questions: Marja Unt, eks@kirjandus.ee. Deadline 1 September 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Writing in Residency
item.description:
Organisation: Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council)

Location: Switzerland-based authors and translators; residencies at partner locations abroad (e.g. Traduki in Southeast Europe, Art Omi).

Award: Travel and accommodation costs (vary by destination); childcare support up to CHF 1,000 per month for applicants with caregiving responsibilities. No application fee.

Duration: Residency to develop or research a project; deadline 1 September.

Deadline: Closed 01 Sep 2026

Pro Helvetia's Writing in Residency programme provides residency opportunities (for example Traduki in Southeast Europe or Art Omi) for authors and translators to develop or research projects. Applicants must have prior professionally published work. ELIGIBILITY: requires a connection to Switzerland (Swiss citizenship, or permanent residency with regular artistic activity in Switzerland); not open to practitioners without a Swiss connection. WHAT IS OFFERED: travel and accommodation costs (varying by destination), plus childcare support of up to CHF 1,000 per month for applicants with caregiving responsibilities. Submission deadline 1 September (23:59 CEST). Apply via the Pro Helvetia portal.

item.title: Jan Michalski Foundation: Writers Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Jan Michalski Foundation for Writing and Literature

Location: Montricher, Switzerland (Swiss Jura, near Lausanne and Geneva)

Award: Weekly allowance of CHF 400, plus travel costs to and from home covered, accommodation in a private cabin, and breakfast and lunch provided. Electric bikes and library access included.

Duration: Two weeks to three months (first 2027 residents arrive mid-January 2027)

Deadline: Closed 31 Aug 2026

Residency for writers and translators at the Jan Michalski Foundation in Montricher, Switzerland, set in seven distinctive 'cabin' modules hanging from an openwork canopy, offering conditions to start, continue or finish a writing project. Around forty authors from around the world (emerging to established) are hosted each year. Open to all kinds of writing and all languages, with priority given to literary writers and translators; other disciplines are welcome as long as literature is at the heart of the project. Residencies are for individuals or pairs working on a common project (e.g. a writer and a translator). A percentage of residencies are dedicated to nature writing. WHAT IS PROVIDED: a private cabin for independent living (a separate cabin per person for pairs; one accessible cabin for reduced mobility), travel costs to and from home, a weekly allowance of CHF 400, breakfast and lunch, electric bikes, and daytime library access. ELIGIBILITY: no age or nationality restrictions; beginners accepted; one application per year; former residents may not reapply (families, children and pets cannot be accommodated). Stays cannot be split into multiple periods. Selection is by a panel chaired by Vera Michalski-Hoffmann, assessing the literary quality of the project, the candidate's background, and whether the stay length matches the project scope. APPLICATION: online in English or French (work excerpts may be in any language); the 2027 form is open 2 June to 31 August 2026; selected candidates announced December 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Archipel Butor Livre de dialogue Creation Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Archipel Butor

Location: Lucinges (74380), Haute-Savoie, France, in the house of the writer Michel Butor.

Award: Creation grant of EUR 2,000 gross per month per artist, so roughly EUR 4,000 each across the two months and EUR 8,000 for the pair. Up to two return journeys per person are covered within France and Europe. Accommodation is provided in Michel Butor's writer's house. No application fee.

Duration: Two months in total, taken as eight weeks that may be split, starting from January 2027. Time is split 70 percent creation and 30 percent mediation activities.

Deadline: Closed 30 Aug 2026

Archipel Butor runs its creation residency out of the former home of the writer Michel Butor in Lucinges, Haute-Savoie, and this call is for a livre de dialogue, a dialogue book made jointly by a writer and a visual artist. The residency exists to give a pair concentrated time to develop a book together and to raise the profile of artist book culture and of collaboration at the centre of artistic process. WHO APPLIES: a pair made up of an author with a project for a dialogue book and a visual artist collaborating on it. The two do not need to have worked together before, but both must be present during the shared periods. WHAT IS PROVIDED: EUR 2,000 gross per month per artist, up to two return trips per person within France and Europe, and accommodation in the writer's house. STRUCTURE: two months in total, taken as eight weeks which may be split across the year from January 2027, with 70 percent of the time given to creation and 30 percent to mediation and public engagement activities. A videoconference is held with the selected laureates beforehand to arrange on-site scheduling and the mediation sessions. HOW TO APPLY: follow the official call document downloadable from the residency page, submitting a single PDF to accueil@archipel-butor.fr containing a joint letter, biographies of both practitioners, the artistic proposal, technical specifications and the proposed mediation activities. NOTE: the call and application file are in French. Deadline 30 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Giancarlo DiTrapano Foundation: The Finch Manuscript Lab 2026
item.description:
Organisation: The Giancarlo DiTrapano Foundation for Literature and the Arts

Location: Finch Country House, Serramezzana, Italy; open to legal residents of the 39 Culture Moves Europe eligible countries, excluding Italy

Award: EUR 2,280 stipend for the residency period (EUR 30 per day in residence, paid weekly), plus travel allowance of EUR 400 (under 5,000 km) or EUR 800 (over 5,000 km), an additional EUR 400 green-travel top-up (e.g. trains instead of planes), and EUR 200 additional support for parents of children under 18. Supported by the Goethe Institute and Culture Moves Europe.

Duration: 2.5 months, 1 October to 15 December 2026

Deadline: Closed 10 Jul 2026

The Finch Manuscript Lab is a 2.5-month residency supporting writers completing book-length manuscripts, hosted at the Finch Country House in Serramezzana, Italy, and designed as the final sprint in the marathon of writing a book. It offers living and work space, writing time in a tranquil setting, creative community, and professional development including manuscript consultations, craft discussions, and publishing seminars. Residency dates: 1 October to 15 December 2026; residents will be selected by 30 July 2026. FUNDING: thanks to the support of the Goethe Institute and Culture Moves Europe, all selected residents receive a stipend of EUR 2,280 for the residency period (EUR 30 per day in residence, paid weekly), a travel allowance of EUR 400 for distances under 5,000 km from Serramezzana or EUR 800 for distances over 5,000 km, an additional EUR 400 for green travel (e.g. taking trains instead of planes), and additional support of EUR 200 for parents of children under 18. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be over 18 and a legal resident of one of the 39 Culture Moves Europe eligible countries, excluding Italy; this includes all EU member states other than Italy and 13 participating non-EU countries (Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, and Tunisia). APPLICATION (via Submittable, in order of importance): a short sample of past work (any length, though only the first 30 pages may be read); a brief note, up to one page, explaining the manuscript or book project to be worked on in residency, where you are in the creation process, and why you are interested; an excerpt of the book project not exceeding 30 pages (prose, poetry, mixed media, photography, or any other form of artist's book is acceptable); and a CV in English. NOTE ON DEADLINE: the foundation's text gives the open call as 15 June to 10 July 2026, while the Submittable page lists a close of Wednesday 15 July 2026 at 12:00 PM; apply by 10 July to be safe.

Open call details

item.title: Designer-Writer Residency 2026-2027 (Centre for Text Margins)
item.description:
Organisation: Centre for Text Margins, Aalto University School of Arts, Design and Architecture (funded by Kone Foundation)

Location: Espoo, Finland

Award: €2,700/month working grant (€32,400 for 12 months)

Duration: 12 months (1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027)

Deadline: Closed 06 May 2026

Twelve-month paid residency for one designer or writer whose practice bridges typography, writing and reading, with a focus on nonlinear, experimental, accessible or otherwise 'marginal' textual practices. Based at Aalto University in Espoo. Includes desk space, workshop facilities, library and archive access. Requires residence in Finland and regular on-campus engagement, 1-2 public talks and one 5-day workshop for students. MA-level degree or equivalent expertise required; no current student status. Travel and accommodation arranged independently.

Open call details
